scenario: A national handloom fair selects exhibitors if they have either exceptional natural-dye expertise or strong export-readiness. To ensure regional representation, 10% of applicants with neither trait are also admitted as wildcards. The selected exhibitor pool seems to show a negative correlation between natural-dye expertise and export-readiness.

data.description: Selection is based on either of two strengths, with a small wildcard channel from the neither group.

question: Among selected exhibitors, compute (a) P(natural-dye | export-ready, selected), and (b) P(natural-dye | not export-ready, selected). Is the apparent negative association between natural-dye expertise and export-readiness real or induced by selection?

ground_truth.explanation: The two capabilities are independent in the population, but selecting on either one creates a spurious negative association in the exhibitor pool.

naive_answer: Export-ready exhibitors seem less likely to have natural-dye expertise, so the two capabilities probably trade off in practice.
naive_trap: The fair selects on either capability, so conditioning on selection induces a false negative relationship between them.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: P(natural-dye | export-ready, selected) = 1120/14000 = 0.08. Step 2: Among not-export selected exhibitors, natural-dye only = 6880 and wildcard neither = 7912, so P(natural-dye | not export, selected) = 6880/(6880+7912) = 0.4652. Step 3: The observed negative association is a selection artifact.
